examples.ko: 이 가게는 변칙 영업으로 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: This shop got into trouble for its irregular business practices.
The exam questions came up in an unusual way, so I was flustered.

examples.ko: 규칙에는 변칙이 있어서 따로 외워야 해요.
examples.en: The rule has exceptions, so you have to memorize them separately.
If you change the schedule in an irregular way, everyone gets inconvenienced.

examples.ko: 한국어 동사에는 변칙 활용이 많아서 어려워요.
examples.en: Korean verbs have many irregular conjugations, so they are hard.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 변칙 작전을 써서 경기를 이겼어요.
examples.en: That team won the game by using an unconventional strategy.

explain: '원칙'과 반대로 정해진 규칙에서 벗어난 방식을 말해요. 문법에서는 보통 '불규칙'이라고 하고, 운영이나 거래 이야기에서는 편법 같은 부정적인 느낌으로 '변칙 운영'처럼 써요. '변칙적으로'처럼 '-적'을 붙인 형태도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '원칙' (principle) and refers to a way that departs from the set rules. In grammar people usually say '불규칙', while in talk about operations or deals it carries a negative, workaround feel, as in '변칙 운영'. The '-적' form '변칙적으로' is also common.

examples.en: This company moved its base to Busan.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 본거지인 서울을 떠나 제주에서 살아요.
examples.en: That singer left Seoul, his home base, and lives on Jeju.
A football team's base is the city where its stadium is.
This place is our club's home base.
This area has been a base for merchants since long ago.
Where would be a good place for our new base?

explain: '본사'는 회사에만 쓰지만 '본거지'는 팀, 모임, 단체, 사람처럼 활동의 중심이 되는 곳에 폭넓게 써요. 뉴스에서는 어떤 단체의 활동 중심지를 가리킬 때 나오고, 일상에서는 '아지트'나 '근거지'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: '본사' is only for companies, but '본거지' is used widely for the center of activity of a team, club, group or person. In the news it names the main place where a group operates, and in daily talk people may also say '아지트' or '근거지'.

examples.en: Citizens denounced the company's wrongdoing online.

examples.ko: 친구들이 모여서 새 규정을 성토하고 있어요.
examples.en: My friends have gathered and are venting about the new rules.
Residents protested, condemning the construction noise.

examples.ko: 회의 분위기가 갑자기 상사를 성토하는 자리로 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: The meeting suddenly turned into a session of slamming the boss.

examples.ko: 팬들이 구단 결정을 성토해도 달라지는 건 없었어요.
examples.en: Even though fans condemned the club's decision, nothing changed.

examples.ko: 점심시간에 동료들과 사장님을 성토한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once bad-mouthed the boss with my coworkers during lunch.

explain: '비난하다'보다 여럿이 모여서 목소리를 높여 잘못을 따진다는 느낌이 강해요. 뉴스, 집회, 온라인 글에서 많이 나오고, 일상에서는 '욕하다'나 '따지다'처럼 말하기도 해요. 'A를 성토하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '비난하다', it has a stronger feel of people gathering and raising their voices to call out a wrong. It appears in news, rallies and online posts, while in everyday talk people may say '욕하다' or '따지다'. It is used with '을/를', as in 'A를 성토하다'.

examples.ko: 경찰은 이번 주 안에 사건 송치를 마칠 계획이에요.
examples.en: The police plan to finish forwarding the case within this week.
After the transfer, the prosecution takes over the case.
The transfer was delayed, so the announcement of results was postponed too.
I saw the news about the case being sent to the prosecution.
I heard whether it will be forwarded will be decided next week.
The paperwork procedure for forwarding is more complicated than I thought.

explain: 일상에서 물건을 '보내다'처럼 쓰지 않고, 경찰이 수사한 사건을 검찰로 넘길 때 주로 써요. 뉴스에서 '검찰 송치'라는 말로 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is not used like '보내다' for everyday items; it is mainly used when the police pass an investigated case on to the prosecution. You often see it in the news as '검찰 송치'.

examples.en: The police sent the case to the prosecution yesterday.

examples.ko: 수사를 마치면 곧 서류를 송치할 거예요.
examples.en: Once the investigation is over, they will forward the documents soon.
I heard the department in charge decided to forward the case.
The police have not forwarded the case yet.

examples.ko: 사건을 먼저 송치해야 다음 단계로 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: The case has to be forwarded first before moving to the next step.

examples.ko: 어제 송치한 사건은 아직 검토 중이에요.
examples.en: The case forwarded yesterday is still under review.

explain: 주어는 보통 경찰이고, '사건을 검찰에/검찰로 송치하다'처럼 써요. 뉴스에서는 '검찰에 송치됐다'처럼 피동으로도 자주 나오지만, 말할 때는 이렇게 능동형으로 익혀 두면 충분해요.
explain_en: The subject is usually the police, as in '사건을 검찰에/검찰로 송치하다'. The news also uses the passive form like '검찰에 송치됐다', but learning this active form is enough for speaking.

examples.en: In the historical drama, the hero was unjustly branded a traitor.
He was called a traitor who betrayed the king.
It was an era when even a traitor's family was punished.

examples.ko: 역적이 되고 싶은 사람은 아무도 없어요.
examples.en: Nobody wants to become a traitor.
This drama is a story about a traitor.

examples.ko: 친구가 약속을 어겼다고 저를 역적 취급해요.
examples.en: My friend treats me like a traitor because I broke a promise.

explain: 옛날에 나라나 왕을 배신한 사람을 가리켜서 사극에서 많이 들어요. '반역자'보다 사극 느낌이 강하고, 요즘은 약속을 어긴 친구에게 농담으로 '이 역적아' 하고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to someone who betrayed the country or the king in the old days, and you hear it a lot in historical dramas. It feels more like period-drama speech than '반역자', and today people sometimes joke '이 역적아' to a friend who broke a promise.

examples.en: These days working through the night is nothing out of the ordinary.
That person tells lies without a second thought.
The current situation is no ordinary problem.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 길이 막히는 건 예사였어요.
examples.en: With heavy snow, traffic jams were a common thing.

examples.ko: 그 사람 표정이 예사롭지 않아서 걱정됐어요.
examples.en: His expression was out of the ordinary, so I was worried.

examples.ko: 공부하다 졸기는 예사인데 오늘은 정말 졸려요.
examples.en: Dozing off while studying is normal for me, but today I'm really sleepy.

explain: '~는 게 예사다'는 늘 있는 흔한 일이라는 말이고, '예사로'는 아무렇지 않게라는 뜻으로 부정적인 행동 앞에 자주 와요. '예사롭다'는 보통 '예사롭지 않다'로 써서 평소와 다르다는 느낌을 줘요.
explain_en: '~는 게 예사다' says something is a common, regular thing, and '예사로' means doing something as if it were nothing, often before a negative action. '예사롭다' is usually used as '예사롭지 않다' to say something is out of the ordinary.

en: make a fool of; toy with

examples.ko: 손님을 우롱하는 광고에 많은 사람이 화가 났어요.
examples.en: Many people were angry at the ad that made fools of customers.
Are you making a fool of me right now?

examples.ko: 그 회사는 소비자를 우롱했다는 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: That company was criticized for toying with consumers.

examples.ko: 우롱하지 마세요. 저도 참을 만큼 참았어요.
examples.en: Don't make a fool of me. I've put up with it long enough.
Everyone was disappointed in the employee who made a fool of the customer.
I had no intention at all of making a fool of the other person.

explain: '놀리다'보다 훨씬 강해서, 상대를 속이거나 바보 취급하며 가지고 노는 느낌이에요. 항의나 뉴스에서 주로 나오고, 일상 말로는 '가지고 놀다'라고 하기도 해요. 당하는 쪽에서는 '우롱당하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '놀리다', carrying the feel of deceiving someone or treating them like a fool and playing with them. It mostly appears in complaints and the news, and in daily talk people may say '가지고 놀다'. From the victim's side it is '우롱당하다'.

examples.en: After a good rest, I got my energy back.
After taking a tonic, my vitality recovered a lot.
My grandmother is still full of vigor.

examples.ko: 몸살을 앓고 나서 원기도 없고 입맛도 없어요.
examples.en: After being sick with body aches, I have no energy and no appetite.
I heard this food is good for restoring vitality.
The children greeted us in voices full of energy.

explain: 몸의 기운을 말해서 아프거나 지친 뒤 회복하는 이야기, 나이 드신 분의 건강 이야기에 잘 나와요. '원기를 회복하다', '원기 왕성하다'처럼 짝으로 익혀 두세요. 평소 말에서는 '기운'이라고 더 많이 해요.
explain_en: It refers to physical energy and often comes up when talking about recovering after illness or fatigue, or about the health of elderly people. Learn it in set pairs like '원기를 회복하다' and '원기 왕성하다'. In everyday speech people more often say '기운'.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 은밀히 만나서 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: The two of them met secretly and made a plan.

examples.ko: 친구가 은밀히 저한테 비밀을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend quietly told me a secret.
It was done in secret, so nobody knew.

examples.ko: 그는 은밀히 회사를 그만둘 준비를 했어요.
examples.en: He secretly prepared to quit the company.
I could hear all the whispering that was meant to be secret.

examples.ko: 은밀히 들어가 보니 방 안에 아무도 없었어요.
examples.en: When I slipped in quietly, there was no one in the room.

explain: '몰래'와 비슷하지만 '몰래'가 일상 대화에 더 가깝고, '은밀히'는 글이나 뉴스에서 조용하고 신중하게 남이 모르게 하는 느낌으로 써요. 형용사 '은밀하다'에서 나온 부사예요.
explain_en: It is similar to '몰래', but '몰래' fits everyday talk better, while '은밀히' is more at home in writing and news, with a feel of doing something quietly and carefully out of others' sight. It is the adverb form of the adjective '은밀하다'.

en: selection of a right person; choice of a right person

examples.ko: 새 대표의 인선이 다음 주에 발표돼요.
examples.en: The selection of the new CEO will be announced next week.

examples.ko: 이번 인선은 결과를 보고 평가해야 해요.
examples.en: This choice of person should be judged by the results.
Opinions were divided over who to pick for the committee.

examples.ko: 인선에 시간이 오래 걸려서 일정이 미뤄졌어요.
examples.en: The selection took a long time, so the schedule was pushed back.

examples.ko: 후임 인선 작업이 아직 끝나지 않았어요.
examples.en: The work of choosing a successor is not finished yet.

examples.ko: 인선 기준을 먼저 정하는 게 좋겠어요.
examples.en: It would be better to set the selection criteria first.

explain: 장관, 대표, 위원처럼 중요한 자리에 알맞은 사람을 골라 정하는 일이라서 뉴스에서 주로 나와요. 일반 직원을 뽑을 때는 '채용'이나 '선발'을 써요. '후임 인선', '인선 작업'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is about choosing a suitable person for an important post such as a minister, head or committee member, so it mostly appears in the news. For hiring ordinary staff, use '채용' or '선발'. It is common in phrases like '후임 인선' and '인선 작업'.

en: select a right person; choose a right person

examples.en: The president selected a new minister.
You must be fair when choosing committee members.
The head decided to pick the team leader personally.
No one has been chosen as the successor yet.

examples.ko: 후임을 인선하는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to choose the successor.
Since the pick was made carefully, I'm looking forward to the results.

explain: 목적어로는 장관, 대표, 위원 같은 높은 자리를 맡을 사람이나 그 자리가 와요. '발탁하다'와 비슷하지만 인선은 적임자를 가려 정한다는 점이 중심이에요. '인선을 하다'처럼 명사로 풀어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Its object is the person for a high post such as a minister, head or committee member, or the post itself. It is close to '발탁하다', but the focus is on picking the right person for the job. You can also say '인선을 하다' using the noun.

examples.ko: 새 사장이 오면서 회사 분위기가 일신했어요.
examples.en: With the new president, the company's atmosphere was completely renewed.

examples.ko: 가게 간판을 바꿔 이미지를 일신하려고 해요.
examples.en: I'm trying to refresh the shop's image by changing the sign.
Make a fresh start with a renewed mind.

examples.ko: 이번 여행이 기분을 일신하는 계기가 되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope this trip becomes a chance to refresh my mood.
Now that the classroom has been spruced up, the students like it too.

examples.ko: 낡은 제도를 일신해야 한다는 의견이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say the outdated system must be overhauled.

explain: '바꾸다'보다 격식 있는 말로, 분위기, 이미지, 제도, 마음가짐을 완전히 새롭게 한다는 느낌이에요. '분위기가 일신하다'처럼 자동사로도, '이미지를 일신하다'처럼 타동사로도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '확 바꾸다'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a more formal word than '바꾸다', with the feel of making an atmosphere, image, system or mindset completely new. It works both intransitively ('분위기가 일신하다') and transitively ('이미지를 일신하다'). In daily conversation people may say '확 바꾸다'.

examples.en: I volunteered to give the presentation first.
He took on the hard job of his own accord.
Nobody volunteered to be team leader.
My brother offered to do the dishes, so I just left it to him.

examples.ko: 내가 자청하고 나선 일이니 끝까지 해야죠.
examples.en: I stepped up for this myself, so I have to see it through.

examples.ko: 청소를 자청한 친구 덕분에 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the friend who volunteered to clean, it finished quickly.

explain: 남이 시키기 전에 스스로 나서서 맡는다는 점에서 '자원하다'와 비슷해요. 힘들거나 책임이 따르는 일에 특히 잘 어울리고, '발표를 자청하다', '자청해서 하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '자원하다' in that you step forward on your own before anyone asks. It suits tasks that are hard or carry responsibility, as in '발표를 자청하다' or '자청해서 하다'.

examples.en: The judge decided after taking various circumstances into account.

examples.ko: 학생의 사정을 참작하면 한 번 더 기회를 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we take the student's situation into account, we can give one more chance.
There was a reason worth taking into account.

examples.ko: 의견을 참작하되 최종 결정은 제가 할게요.
examples.en: I'll take your opinion into account, but I'll make the final decision.
Even taking his age into account, that behavior was wrong.
My teacher took my situation into consideration for me.

explain: '고려하다'와 비슷하지만 상대의 사정을 헤아려서 조금 봐준다는 느낌이 있어요. 판결, 평가, 벌을 말할 때 자주 나오고 '정상을 참작하다'가 대표적인 표현이에요. 보통 '사정, 상황, 의견'이 목적어로 와요.
explain_en: It is similar to '고려하다', but it carries a feel of understanding someone's circumstances and going a bit easier on them. It often appears in talk of verdicts, evaluations and punishment, and '정상을 참작하다' is a typical expression. Its object is usually things like circumstances, situation or opinions.

examples.ko: 이번 대회는 초유의 관객 수를 기록했어요.
examples.en: This tournament recorded an unprecedented number of spectators.
All the staff were flustered by the unprecedented situation.

examples.ko: 한국 역사상 초유의 일이라 뉴스에 계속 나와요.
examples.en: It's the first time in Korean history, so it keeps coming up in the news.

examples.ko: 그 회사가 올해 초유의 위기를 맞았어요.
examples.en: That company faced an unprecedented crisis this year.
An unprecedented blackout left the whole city in darkness.
In an unprecedented situation like this, you need to stay calm.

explain: 거의 '초유의 + 명사' 형태로 쓰고, '초유' 혼자 쓰는 일은 드물어요. 사태, 위기, 기록처럼 큰 일 앞에 붙고 뉴스에서 자주 볼 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '전례 없는', '사상 처음'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '초유의 + noun' and rarely stands alone. It attaches to big things like incidents, crises and records, and you often see it in the news. Similar expressions are '전례 없는' and '사상 처음'.

examples.ko: 신하는 왕의 총애를 받아 높은 자리에 올랐어요.
examples.en: The minister won the king's favor and rose to a high position.

examples.ko: 왕의 총애가 깊어서 다른 신하들이 질투했어요.
examples.en: The king's favor was so deep that the other ministers were jealous.

examples.ko: 선생님의 총애를 받던 학생이 상을 탔어요.
examples.en: The student who was the teacher's favorite won a prize.
I was always careful, afraid of losing his favor.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 감독의 총애 속에 성장했어요.
examples.en: That actor grew up under the director's special favor.

examples.ko: 사극에서 후궁이 왕의 총애를 두고 다퉈요.
examples.en: In the historical drama, the royal consorts compete for the king's favor.

explain: 윗사람이 아랫사람을 특별히 아끼는 마음이라서, 일반적인 '사랑'과 달리 방향이 정해져 있어요. '총애를 받다', '총애를 잃다', '총애를 독차지하다'처럼 짝으로 많이 써요. 사극이나 직장 이야기에서 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a special fondness that a superior feels toward someone below, so unlike plain '사랑' it has a set direction. It is commonly used in pairs like '총애를 받다', '총애를 잃다' and '총애를 독차지하다'. You may hear it in historical dramas or talk about the workplace.

examples.en: The king especially favored that minister.
The pupil the teacher favors was chosen as the representative.
The boss dotes on the youngest who works well.
The granddaughter my grandfather doted on got married.

examples.ko: 윗사람이 한 사람만 총애하면 팀 분위기가 나빠져요.
examples.en: If a superior favors only one person, the team atmosphere gets worse.
She is a child so diligent that the teachers dote on her.

explain: 윗사람이 아랫사람을 특별히 아낄 때 쓰기 때문에, 학생이 선생님께 쓰면 어색해요. 같은 마음을 일상에서는 '아끼다'나 '예뻐하다'로 말해요. 반대로 받는 쪽에서는 '총애를 받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a superior especially cherishes someone below, so it sounds odd if a student says it about a teacher. In daily speech the same feeling is expressed with '아끼다' or '예뻐하다'. From the receiving side, you say '총애를 받다'.

examples.ko: 옛날 사람들은 산 위에 성을 축조했어요.
examples.en: People in the old days built a fortress on top of the mountain.

examples.ko: 이 다리는 백 년 전에 축조한 거예요.
examples.en: This bridge was built a hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 둑을 축조하는 데 오랜 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to build the embankment.

examples.ko: 튼튼하게 축조해야 홍수에도 견딜 수 있어요.
examples.en: It has to be built solidly to withstand floods.
The government decided to build a new harbor.
It was constructed by stacking bricks, but it collapsed soon.

explain: '짓다'보다 딱딱한 말로, 성, 둑, 다리처럼 쌓아서 만드는 큰 구조물에 어울려요. 집이나 건물은 일상에서 '짓다'를 쓰고, 축조는 설명문이나 역사 이야기에서 주로 나와요. 피동은 '축조되다'예요.
explain_en: It is a stiffer word than '짓다', suited to large structures built up by stacking, such as fortresses, embankments and bridges. For houses and buildings people say '짓다' in daily life, and '축조' mostly appears in explanatory texts and history. The passive form is '축조되다'.

examples.ko: 인력 충원이 급해서 채용 공고를 냈어요.
examples.en: We urgently need more staff, so we posted a job notice.
We asked for more staff, but I heard the budget is short.

examples.ko: 이번 충원에서 열 명을 뽑을 계획이에요.
examples.en: We plan to take on ten people in this round of staffing.
We have to redo the staffing plan first.

examples.ko: 직원 충원 없이 일하려니 너무 힘들어요.
examples.en: Working without any added staff is really hard.
A vacancy opened up, so we started the process of filling it.

explain: '채용'은 사람을 새로 뽑는 일이고, '충원'은 부족하거나 빈 자리를 채운다는 점이 달라요. 회사, 학교, 팀 이야기에서 '인력 충원', '결원 충원'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '채용' is hiring people anew, while '충원' stresses filling a shortage or an empty spot. It is used in talk about companies, schools and teams, as in '인력 충원' and '결원 충원'.

examples.en: The company filled its staff shortage.

examples.ko: 올해 안에 직원 다섯 명을 충원할 예정이에요.
examples.en: We plan to add five employees within this year.
The team can only run if it adds players.
It took time to fill the vacancy.

examples.ko: 아직 충원하지 못해서 모두 야근을 해요.
examples.en: We haven't been able to add staff yet, so everyone works overtime.

examples.ko: 새로 충원한 사람들이 잘 적응하고 있어요.
examples.en: The newly added people are adjusting well.

explain: '보충하다'는 물건이나 내용에도 쓰지만 '충원하다'는 사람, 즉 인원이나 인력을 채울 때만 써요. '인력을 충원하다', '결원을 충원하다'처럼 목적어가 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: '보충하다' can be used for things or content too, but '충원하다' is only for filling people, meaning headcount or manpower. Its objects are fixed, as in '인력을 충원하다' and '결원을 충원하다'.

examples.en: Residents submitted a petition to city hall.
Could you sign the petition?

examples.ko: 탄원서에는 이름과 사정이 자세히 적혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The petition had names and circumstances written in detail.
The neighbors gathered and wrote the petition together.
Thanks to the petition, the problem was solved quickly.
Where should I submit the petition?

explain: 억울한 사정을 알리고 도움이나 선처를 바라는 글이라서, 단순히 신청하는 '신청서'와 달리 호소하는 내용이 중심이에요. '탄원서를 내다/쓰다/제출하다/서명하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a written appeal that explains an unfair situation and asks for help or leniency, so unlike a plain application form ('신청서'), its core is the appeal. It is used as '탄원서를 내다/쓰다/제출하다/서명하다'.

examples.ko: 그 왕은 백성을 괴롭힌 폭군으로 기억돼요.
examples.en: That king is remembered as a tyrant who tormented his people.
Once the tyrant was gone, the country became calm.

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 폭군 같아서 다들 무서워해요.
examples.en: Our team leader is like a tyrant, so everyone is afraid of him.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 읽은 동화에 폭군이 나와요.
examples.en: A tyrant appears in a fairy tale I read as a child.
The tyrant's son became king.

examples.ko: 집에서 폭군처럼 굴지 않는 아빠가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be a dad who doesn't act like a tyrant at home.

explain: 역사나 드라마에서 나쁜 왕을 가리킬 때 자주 쓰고, 일상에서는 무섭게 구는 상사나 부모를 과장해서 '폭군 같다'고 말하기도 해요. '독재자'는 권력을 혼자 쥔 정치 이야기에 쓰고, '폭군'은 난폭하고 잔인한 성격이 더 중심이에요.
explain_en: It is often used for a bad king in history or dramas, and in daily life people exaggerate by saying a scary boss or parent is '폭군 같다'. '독재자' is for politics where one person holds all power, while '폭군' focuses more on a violent, cruel character.

examples.en: I give an offering at church every Sunday.

examples.ko: 헌금이 모여서 새 건물을 지을 수 있었어요.
examples.en: The offerings added up, and a new building could be built.
I wrote my name on the offering envelope and handed it in.

examples.ko: 헌금은 각자 형편에 맞게 내는 거예요.
examples.en: Offerings are given according to each person's means.
We helped neighbors in need with the collected offerings.
During the offering time, the children put in coins.

explain: 주로 교회나 절 같은 종교 단체에 내는 돈을 말해요. 일반적인 기부는 '기부금'이라고 하고, 어려운 사람을 돕는 돈은 '성금'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It mainly means money given to a religious group such as a church or temple. General giving is called '기부금', and money to help people in need is called '성금'.

examples.en: Church members donated for the church's construction.
I give part of my salary as an offering every month.
I haven't decided yet how much to give.
Many people give offerings out of gratitude.
After giving the offering, I felt at ease.
They set up a scholarship with the money my friend donated.

explain: '기부하다'와 비슷하지만 종교 단체에 돈을 낼 때 주로 써요. 일반 단체나 학교에 돈을 낼 때는 '기부하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is similar to '기부하다', but it is mainly used for giving money to a religious organization. For ordinary organizations or schools, '기부하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: This hotel room is truly luxurious.
Once you get used to a luxurious life, it's hard to go back.
It looks lavish, but the price is surprisingly cheap.
I don't want to have a lavish wedding.
It's not luxurious, but it's a clean room.
The once-luxurious old mansion is a museum now.

explain: '사치스럽다'와 비슷해요. 방, 음식, 생활처럼 눈에 보이는 것이 값비싸고 화려할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '고급스럽다'나 '사치스럽다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '호사스럽다'는 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말에서 들려요.
explain_en: It is close to '사치스럽다'. It is used when visible things like rooms, food or lifestyles are expensive and splendid. In daily conversation people more often say '고급스럽다' or '사치스럽다', while '호사스럽다' is heard in writing or somewhat formal speech.

examples.ko: 정치에 환멸을 느껴서 뉴스를 안 봐요.
examples.en: I'm disillusioned with politics, so I don't watch the news.
After long expectations, only disillusionment was left.

examples.ko: 직장 생활에 환멸이 와서 쉬고 싶어요.
examples.en: I've become disenchanted with work life and want to take a break.
I quit that job because of my disillusionment.
The gap between ideal and reality led to disillusionment.
As my disillusionment deepened, my motivation vanished too.

explain: '실망'보다 강해서, 믿고 기대했던 사람, 제도, 일에 정이 떨어질 만큼 실망했을 때 써요. '환멸을 느끼다'가 가장 기본이 되는 짝이에요. '환멸감'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is stronger than '실망' and is used when you were so let down by a person, system or job you trusted that you lose all affection for it. '환멸을 느끼다' is the most basic pairing. It can also be said as '환멸감'.
